Our Team:

We are a team of high schoolers who are ambitious about exploring space, medicine and improve their skill sets. Our goal by joining NASA Space Apps Challenge is to apply our critical thinking skills and show some serious teamwork to demonstrate a creative and useful way to solve this challenge.
summary:
CREWGUARD is a software prototype to monitor astronaut health designed for long space missions and it can work offline. It has four different modes to adapt to different environments: crew capsule, orbital station, lunar base and Mars habitat.

It's monitoring engine looks for changes which are persistent or indicating emergency., while also detecting unreliable data thorugh not connected sensors and looking at time stamps. When an alert appears, CREWGUARD explains the indicators and provides a specific response checklist. Crew members can understand what is happening and learn what to do, while also recording actions and documenting reassessments. 

CREWGUARD also includes trends of health history, data backups, offline access and a NASA OSDR research section. 

CREWGUARD connects monitoring with understandable and easy to track guidance and crew recorded follow-up.  demonstrates how astronauts could better review health information and document their response when communication and medical support may be limited.

All operational readings and alert thresholds in this prototype are simulated. It is not a medical device and does not replace approved mission procedures or medical personnel.
details:
CREWGUARD is a software designed to monitor health status of astronauts. It supports crew wellbeing and health awareness during space missions. It is important to monitor the health of the astronauts as human space exploration moves towards longer missions, esspecially to Mars. The medium of space missions differ and it creates different challenges, that' s why a single monitoring system won' t be enough for every situation.

CREWGUARD addresses this by providing one adaptable dashboard with four mission profiles: Rocket/Crew Capsule, Orbital Space Station, Lunar Base and Mars Mission/Habitat. Each profile has different monitoring priorities according to its situation.

Our application shows some health categories, such as physical health, mental wellbeing, radiation exposure and environmental conditions. It presents measurements such as heart rate, blood pressure, sleep duration, fatigue, exercise, oxygen levels, cabin pressure, temperature and radiation exposure. Users are able to record daily health check-ins, review historical measurements and monitor changes over time.

One of the most crucial feature is it can detect anomalies with a system that compares measurements against personal datas. It can identify persistent unusual trends, multiple changing indicators, disconnected sensors and emergency demonstration scenarios. System provides alerts with colours that show the risk level of alert, supports evidence in order to explain the alert and suggests what to do next. This system helps users to understand the measurement which requires attention and further process.

Another important feature is its offline-first design. CREWGUARD is able to record the measurements when it' s offline as well. It uses local browser storage to preserve datas of astronauts and designed as an installable Progressive Web App. This is particularly relevant to deep-space missions, where communication with Earth may be delayed or temporarily unavailable.

We developed CREWGUARD using React, TypeScript, Vite and CSS. We used Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot Agent during development. IndexedDB is used for local data storage, while a service worker supports offline application access. The current prototype uses simulated sensor measurements and does not require physical hardware.

What makes CREWGUARD creative is its combination of mission-specific monitoring, physical and mental health indicators, environmental awareness, anomaly detection and offline functionality within a single application. Rather than assuming that every astronaut has the same monitoring needs, it adapts its priorities to four distinct mission environments.

Throughout development, we considered the differences between mission environments, limited communication during deep-space travel, sensor availability, data freshness, local data privacy and the importance of presenting alerts clearly. We also considered medical safety: CREWGUARD is intended as a monitoring and awareness tool, not a diagnostic system or a replacement for professional medical judgment.

Our long-term vision is to develop CREWGUARD further into a reliable, adaptable health-monitoring platform that could support astronaut wellbeing during future human missions beyond Earth.
